Lurivo is a lure-fishing companion for anglers who plan one outing at the water. Rack your swims and lures, then script this trip's retrieve cadence.
Most of us learn a cadence, get a couple of strikes, and forget the exact count by the next cast. Lurivo holds that count for you. On Shore you photograph a point or import a shot you already have, then tag water and structure. You photograph the boxes you carry and tag kind, weight, and colour. On Twitch you pick one swim, pick the lures for this water, and lay a strip of twitches and pauses. A twitch starts at one second and a pause at three; you retune each beat. You write three cue lines for Nibble, Hooked, and Fighting, then save the outing so it settles into the Outing archive.
When you reach the bank, Cast is the live beat. The cadence you wrote is spoken aloud on the interval you set. Three large buttons still fire those cues if you can tap, and you can also speak nibble, hooked, fighting, end cast, or abandon so the same actions run without looking down. After End cast you can keep a spoken reel note. The strike log and that note stay on the outing you reopen before the next trip — which lure earned more strikes, which cadence you rode.
Rack swims and lure boxes with the tags you actually use
Script a retrieve as a strip of twitches and pauses
Hear the beat spoken, and call strikes by voice or by tap
Keep a spoken reel note that rides with the outing
Cast is the signature: your rhythm called back to you, your cues spoken when a fish shows, your hands left on the rod.
